title: Magic ring granny motif blanket
subtitle: Small 4-round granny motifs joined as you go using the magic ring start.
excerpt: Each granny motif starts from a magic ring and is joined to its neighbours on the final round. The blanket is built motif by motif without a separate joining step.
sourceNotes: Granny square motif from Weldon's Practical Crochet (series 3, 1880s). Magic ring is a modern technique. Join-as-you-go is a modern joining method. Internet Archive.

glossaryTerms.definition: An adjustable loop start. Wind yarn around fingers to make a ring, work stitches into it, then pull the tail to close the centre hole completely.
On the final round of each motif, replace one chain space with a slip stitch into the matching chain space of the adjacent motif. Joins motifs without sewing.
Three trebles worked into the same chain space, forming the basic unit of a granny square or motif.
Threading yarn tails through stitches with the tapestry needle.

crochet.gaugeText: 1 motif = 8 x 8 cm blocked. 11 x 11 motifs = 88 x 88 cm.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Baby blanket, approx 88 x 88 cm (121 motifs).

content.text: A magic ring granny motif blanket is approximately 88 x 88 cm built from 121 small 4-round granny motifs. Each motif starts with a
magic ring
and is joined to its neighbours on round 4 using
join-as-you-go

No sewing is needed to assemble the blanket. Each new motif is attached as its final round is worked. Total yardage is around 800 g in aran. Using two or three colours in rotation gives a scrappy or planned-colour result.
What you need
Each motif (first motif only)
Round 1: Magic ring. Ch 3, 2 tr into ring, ch 2. *3 tr into ring, ch 2*. Repeat 3 times. Sl st to top of ch 3. Pull ring closed. (4 groups of 3 tr with ch 2 corners.)
Round 2: Sl st to corner space. Ch 3, 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr into same space (corner made). *Ch 1, 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr into next corner space*. Repeat 3 times. Ch 1. Sl st. (4 corners, 4 side ch-1 spaces.)
Round 3: Work corners as before. Work 1
granny cluster
into each side ch-1 space. Ch 1 between clusters. Sl st. (4 corners, 8 side clusters.)
Round 4: Repeat Round 3 structure, adding one more cluster to each side. Fasten off.
Each subsequent motif (join-as-you-go)

Work rounds 1-3 as normal. On round 4, when working the side that meets an existing motif: replace each ch-2 corner with ch 1, sl st into matching corner space, ch 1. Replace each ch-1 side gap with sl st into matching ch-1 space. This joins the motifs on the go.
Assembly order
Work in rows of 11 motifs. First row: 11 standalone motifs. Each subsequent motif in row 2 onward joins to the motif above and to the left on round 4.
Edging
Work one round of dc (UK) around the full blanket perimeter. Work 3 dc into each corner of each motif at the outer edge. Work 3 dc into each outer blanket corner.
Finishing
Secure all tails with
weaving in ends
. Block each motif as it is made if using wool. Block the finished blanket flat.
Care
Machine wash 40 degrees normal. Dry flat. The join-as-you-go seams are as strong as the motif stitches.
What to try next
The granny square join blanket uses the same motifs sewn together rather than joined live. Or try the granny stripe baby blanket for a continuous-row approach using granny clusters without motifs.
